focus_points.point: FOR UPDATE is the first statement on the connection (database.connect only opens it, assuming no prior statements in connect). The lock comes before get_log (the photo read).

Every exit path from the inner try rolls back (explicit), and the connection is closed by closing(). New files are removed by the outer except on every failure path including HTTPException; writes are registered in `written` before the open. A failure of lock_log itself (e.g. a DB error) is inside the try too.
Old files are deleted after the with-block (commit done) and only on the success path, since an exception re-raises before that code.

The pg_stat_activity query is scoped with datname = current_database() on a connection to the test DB and excludes its own pid. It counts any Lock waiter in that DB. Can it false-positive? Only if some other session waits on a lock in the test database; in these tests the only possible waiters are the edit threads (the holder never waits), so it is sound. Tuple-lock waiters (the second queued edit) also show wait_event_type='Lock', so n=2 is reachable. Cannot hang: 15s deadline. A very fast waiter that has not yet started its query would just be polled again. Residual risk: the request thread could be counted as blocked while waiting on something unrelated, but nothing else locks in these flows.
No real DB, uploads/ or port 8000 touched, by reading.
No behaviour beyond the spec seen; line lengths under 100; imports used (threading, time, contextmanager, psycopg, make_image, make_log, put, rows, snapshot all referenced). No pyflakes to confirm.

verification.self_critique: Everything about runtime behaviour is unverified. Main unconfirmed risks: (1) TestClient used from several threads at once may serialize requests so that the two-waiter wait_blocked(db, 2) never reaches 2 and the tests fail by timeout (a test-mechanics failure, not a lock defect); (2) the shared `holder` for tests that start two threads relies on both requests having passed _exists before blocking; (3) the implementation notes say 7 tests but there are 8 (documentation nit). The 404 and file-write/DB-failure lock-release paths have no direct test.
